```

hang in 1.6.x or produce valid SQL output?

```

I don't know if it can help, but the full `alembic/` are available from `https://github.com/silenius/amnesia/tree/dev/amnesia/alembic` for the `amnesiacms` branch and from `https://github.com/silenius/amnesia_multilingual/tree/dev/amnesia_multilingual/alembic` for the `multilingual` branch

Awesome, thanks.  Looks like it's somehow related to repeating an identifier in depends_on that's already the down_revision for that script (like below).  I think it's not needed to repeat the dependency but alembic should handle it.  Will look into it!
```
revision = '32b12866f6a2'
down_revision = 'e025de45166e'
branch_labels = None
depends_on = 'e025de45166e'
```

Ah, I see .. it's strange indeed to have the same identifier for a depends_on and a down_revision, it should be a mistake on my side I think..

Thank you for your quick reply and explanations

I can confirm that with:

```diff 
diff --git a/amnesia/alembic/versions/20210503_32b12866f6a2_permissions.py b/amnesia/alembic/versions/20210503_32b12866f6a2_permissions.py
index 998cd5c..0560e3e 100644
--- a/amnesia/alembic/versions/20210503_32b12866f6a2_permissions.py
+++ b/amnesia/alembic/versions/20210503_32b12866f6a2_permissions.py
@@ -14,7 +14,7 @@ import sqlalchemy as sa
 revision = '32b12866f6a2'
 down_revision = 'e025de45166e'
 branch_labels = None
-depends_on = 'e025de45166e'
+depends_on = None
 
 migration_path = Path(__file__)
 migration_sql_path = migration_path.parent.parent / 'sql'
```

it works with 1.6.2

Great!  Glad that worked, thanks for raising this.

@CaselIT I noticed the bug occurs only when `depends_on = 'e025de45166e'`, and not when `depends_on = ('e025de45166e',)`.  Should this give a warning or error here or just handle it transparently (as previous versions evidently did)?

Thanks for looking into it @simonbowly 

I'm not actually sure if both versions are allowed. cc @zzzeek
I would say let's warn, so that things dont break but people are encouraged to repair it. thanks for looking into it!
@simonbowly  did you want me to look at this or do you have something you're planning?

I wanted to ask the same thing.

Also, I was thinking that I'm not sure we should warn for this if it's a string. I mean `down_revision` behalves the same, it can be None, a string or a tuple of strings
it's my bug anyway, it's in the topological sort algo.

**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **master** branch:

**ensure heads remain unique in topological** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/c/sqlalchemy/alembic/+/2835

Nice one, thanks - I was having trouble reproducing this in tests.  There's a related issue when downgrading in this case of duplicated dependencies, I hit this assertion when trying to downgrade the revision in question:

https://github.com/sqlalchemy/alembic/blob/5a277a5d0ee13fd66d389631ac854556921613b8/alembic/runtime/migration.py#L720-L721

Simplest approach I think is to make sure `_all_down_revisions` and `_normalised_down_revisions` are de-duped.

Created a changeset for this but I guess gerrit doesn't link if the issue is closed - can open a separate issue if this needs a more complete description?

https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/c/sqlalchemy/alembic/+/2836

**Simon Bowly** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **master** branch:

**De-duplicate Revision.down_revision helpers.** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/c/sqlalchemy/alembic/+/2836
